update_20260529_pm.new_root_cause: Die & Stripper contacts had Stfac=1.0E-4 (500x SOFTER than punch 5.0E-2). The soft contact lets the steel stripper sink INTO the aluminum (negative energy = penetration), then a surface element inverts -> node ejection. Prior Stfac tests reportedly never persisted (file revert), so this is the FIRST valid test.

update_20260529_pm.stfac_sweep_result: Run102 (5e-2): +20% injection, fail 12.6ms. Run103 (5e-3): +20% injection, fail 12.3ms. Run101 (1e-4): -37% penetration, fail 13.1ms (longest). ALL fail 12-13ms at stripper contact -> contact-stiffness tuning is NOT the fix. Run104 (VC=1.0 damping): solver ran 40x slower (pathological), killed.
update_20260529_pm.ROOT_CAUSE_FOUND_run105: Measured material mesh: 43 Z-levels (~42 element layers) through 0.5mm -> mesh is FINE, NOT coarse. PRIOR 'needs remesh' conclusion was WRONG. Real cause = TETRA4 element FORMULATION: starter .out confirmed ITET4=1000 (linear 1-point tetra) for the aluminum -> severe VOLUMETRIC/SHEAR LOCKING -> material cannot plasticize (explains 'plastic work ~0' anomaly) -> builds elastic energy under stripper contact -> surface node ejects.
update_20260529_pm.fix_itet3: Rewrote /PROP/SOLID/2 (aluminum ONLY) in well-formed radioss2022 format with Itetra4=3 (linear TETRA4 + nodal pressure averaging = anti-locking). Verified via starter echo: Material Itetra4=3.
update_20260529_pm.element_formulation_result: Run105 (Itetra4=3): EXPLODED early at 3.4ms (ERR -99.9%), before any tool contact. Run106 (Itetra4=1, quadratic 4-int-pt): EXPLODED at 6.1ms (+99.9%), fail 8.9ms. BOTH anti-locking tet formulations blow up EARLIER than the locking 1-point default (stable to 13ms).
update_20260529_pm.DEFINITIVE_CONCLUSION: FUNDAMENTAL CONFLICT confirmed: (1) the fine unstructured TETRA4 mesh REQUIRES AMS to run at dt=1e-6 (without AMS, CST gave DM/M=3497, prior C2). (2) AMS at dt=1e-6 is ONLY stable with the locking-prone 1-point tetra (Itetra4=1000). (3) The anti-locking formulations (Itetra4=1/3) need a far smaller timestep and explode under AMS. => The TETRA4 volumetric/shear LOCKING that causes the ~13ms stripper-contact node ejection CANNOT be removed by any .rad parameter, because the only locking-free option is incompatible with the AMS the mesh requires. This is a genuine mesh-architecture limitation, not a tuning gap.
what_actually_fixes_it: REMESH the workpiece with well-shaped HEXA (or sweep/structured) elements: a coarser, regular hex mesh has a far larger natural timestep -> no extreme AMS needed -> can use Isolid=14/24 (locking-free hexa) which plasticizes correctly. This is the single highest-value fix and requires HyperMesh/preprocessor on the CAD.
If staying with tets: regenerate as TETRA10 (quadratic) AND drop AMS for a proper /DT/NODA/CST, accepting longer runtime. Requires remesh.
Verify die slug-relief so the cut slug is not crushed (fix D) - only matters once the >13ms barrier is passed.
